title: GitPoint
description: Build a GitHub-oriented repository and issue browser with API mapping, search/filtering, cached state, and clear authentication limits.
problem: Learners need a source-grounded way to understand and extend GitPoint while separating implemented behavior from demo data, simulations, and missing integrations.
audience: Third-year undergraduate students who have completed introductory programming and want a practical mobile mini-project.
prerequisites: Git basics and ability to run the platform tooling described in the source README
learning_outcomes: Explain and trace repository/issue shapes, response mapping, sample data, and sort fields in its named source files.
Explain and trace fetch client, request paths, headers, response mapping, githuberror, and rate-limit headers in its named source files.
Explain and trace search fields, date ordering, state filters, and list rendering in its named source files.
Explain and trace cache keys, load/save, corrupt data, provider startup, and fallback state in its named source files.
Explain and trace context lifecycle, tabs, profile/repository/issue states, and reusable controls in its named source files.
Explain and trace mock response evidence, test script, public api boundary, and token risk in its named source files.
Distinguish unit-test evidence from device, service, and deployment evidence.
Propose a safe, bounded extension without describing it as already implemented.
